title: Visualizing Interfacial Structure and Reaction Behaviour of Li-Chalcogen Batteries
content: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) have played a pivotal role in the transition to renewable energy, powering applications from electric vehicles (EVs) to grid-scale energy storage systems. However, the increasing demand for higher energy density and cost-effective battery technologies necessitates the development of next-generation energy storage systems capable of achieving an energy density of 500 Wh kg⁻¹ by 2030. Chalcogen elements (O, S, Se, Te) from Group 16 of the periodic table offer unique potential due to their ability to undergo multi-electron transfer reactions and significantly enhancing energy density [1,2]. Despite this promise, Li-chalcogen batteries face critical scientific challenges, including the dissolution and shuttle effect of lithium polyspecies (e.g., polysulfides, polyselenides, and polytellurides), ambiguous reaction pathways, and transient solid-phase intermediates formed during discharge.
